# Autonomy architecture: strategy review 1 of 3 (Ember 0.13.0, `ab713b0`)

**Sources.**
- Code at `ab713b0`. Paths are relative to `ember/app/`.
- The first analysis: §1, §3, §7 and §10.
- Report **A** = `281e8edf-…-141055.txt` (0.12.0, 12:10 UTC).
- Report **B** = `fdd5866d-…-171054.txt` (0.13.0, 15:10 UTC). Its EVENTS go back to 09-28 14:37.

**Labels:**
- **live:** it appears in a report;
- **code:** found by reading the code;
- **reproduced:** a scratch test run against the real code with the app's venv, kept outside the repo;
- **inferred:** worked out from indirect evidence;
- **judgement:** my own view.

**One caveat shapes everything below.** Before B was taken:
- 0.12.0 ran 4 live cycles (#42–#45) and 0.13.0 ran one (#46, which was stopped).
- The two behaviour releases were installed 6.5 hours apart on 09-30 (08:17 and 14:52, B events). There were 77 commits and 44 migrations in the ~21 hours since 0.11.1 (`git rev-list 4f31ccc..ab713b0`).
- Every Phase C–E table is still empty: `venture_cases`, `desk_picks`, `predictions`, `agenda`, `action_journal`, `policy_grants` and `policy_uses` all hold 0 rows (B:180-187).

So nothing live yet shows whether the delegation, agenda or decision tooling works. My verdicts on them rest on the code and on reproductions.

---

## 1. Verdict

- **In code, the backbone the first analysis asked for now exists:**
  - milestones graded by metrics;
  - a money goal and listing tests set by Ember's code;
  - stage rules with kill dates;
  - cycle digests and an obligations ledger;
  - burn modes;
  - a policy engine with NEVER enforced twice (code and DB), a journal, Undo, and a switch that takes back every unlock.

  This is a real change from 0.11.1, where "the entrepreneurial part is prompt text that no code checks".
- **In live use, the owner is still the approver, QA, scheduler and strategist:**
  - he clicked 12 of 12 Etsy requests;
  - he did QA or art direction 5 times in 2 days;
  - he triggered 5 of the last 12 cycles;
  - he switched off both owner wake options;
  - he reset the guard's cost scale by hand;
  - he fed research into the Library himself (4 documents);
  - he picked the POD provider over the agent's recommendation.
- **The delegation half of the policy engine is not usable as built** (§5):
  - Unlocks are keyed to the milestone the plan says it is aiming at (reproduced).
  - An unlock stops working, without notice, once its milestone is met.
  - The rules fit 2 of 13 live requests, and none of the kinds that dominate the next month.
  - The word filter for tax and contracts catches product copy.
  - Promotions can't be reached.

  The safety half (NEVER, revocation, audit, Undo) is right and should stay.
- **The event model is sound as data, not as a wake policy** (§6). The owner's own clicks start full, uncoalesced cycles, and he turned both options off after bursts of them. That is the clearest signal in the data: he wants Ember to work on its own clock, and not to spend money because he clicked something.
- **What stands in the way now:**
  1. delegation that doesn't fit the real requests;
  2. quality judgement that still lives in the prompt, so the owner does it;
  3. money: code-set **maintenance mode arrives in about 1–3 days at $5–7 a day**, which would stall the one backed test;
  4. no market signal: 6 listings have 4 views in total, so no autonomy can yet be earned from results;
  5. a release cadence that leaves no time for live evidence.

  More autonomy code will only help after points 1–3 are fixed.

---

## 2. How far from a fully autonomous worker and entrepreneur

| Level | Meaning | Where Ember is |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Supervised assistant | Plans its own work. Outbound actions, schedule, QA and strategy are the owner's. | 0.11.1 live (first analysis §1) |
| 2. Self-managing operator | Wakes itself, keeps its promises, and measures and grades its results in code. The owner approves outbound actions and sets strategy. | **Code: yes. Live: partly** (5 of 12 recent cycles started by the owner; the owner still does QA) |
| 3. Delegated operator | Carries out routine, reversible actions within budgets the owner sets. The owner approves firsts, new product lines, money and legal matters. | Code has the tools, but they fit about 15% of live requests; 0 unlocks exist |
| 4. Entrepreneur with a mandate | Picks, tests, scales and stops ventures within a money budget. The owner backs or kills ventures, funds them, and handles identity and legal duties. | Decision tools exist in code (numeric case, knock-outs, critic, decision desk, stage rules, predictions). There is no money mandate and no outcome data yet. |
| 5. No owner | — | Not a goal. Accounts, first contacts, legal duties and money stay the owner's (first analysis §10). |

"Fully autonomous" therefore means level 4 for Ember. That matches the owner's own words: "I'm your investor, not your assistant" (B:1431).

| Dimension | 0.11.1 | 0.13.0 in code | 0.12/0.13 live |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outbound actions | all clicked | 5 unlock rules, NEVER, Undo | **12 of 12 Etsy requests clicked; 0 unlocks** (B:1397-1411, B:187) |
| Waking | timer, message, Wake now | adds decisions, agenda events, milestone check wakes, evening reserve | **5 of the last 12 cycles owner-triggered** (#38, #39 and #46 by Wake now; #43 and #44 by decisions); both wake options off (B:130-131) |
| Measuring | the agent's word | metric catalogue, code grading, money goal, day 7/14/21 bars | code set 9 of 13 open milestones (B:1350-1364); nothing graded yet (0–2 views per listing, B:508) |
| Continuity | the model's last reply | digest, obligations, journal written by code | works: #44 and #46 lost their reflection to the guard, and the code wrote the journal and digest (B:1367-1371) |
| Venture decisions | opinions | numeric case, knock-outs, critic, desk, stage rules, predictions | the owner picked POD, then Printify over the agent's Gelato choice (messages #61–#63), then the poster style (#62). READY had one item (B:480-482) |
| Quality | owner | photo count (`qa.MIN_PHOTOS`), dpi, image ratio, word counts | **the owner did QA 5 times in 2 days** (§4) |
| Money | owner records it | burn modes, opt-in automatic revenue, P&L | automatic revenue off (B:58); net runway 18.3 days, burn mode focus (B:413-415) |
| New abilities | workshop → upgrade requests (never used) | same | upgrade #1 (Printify) was requested and shipped in under a day through a coding session (B:1433-1435): the one working growth path |

---

## 3. What moved from prompt to code since 0.11.1, and what is still prompt-only

**Moved to code** (each item is enforced by code or the database, and its prose is gone; `tests/test_rule_audit.py:103-150` lists 15 deleted rules with the tests that prove them):

| Was in the prompt | Now | Commit / where |
|---|---|---|
| Milestones "done" on the agent's word | metric catalogue; code closes done or missed; a DB trigger refuses the agent's "done" | `08e735d`; `agent/metrics.py:482` |
| "Put promises on the roadmap" | money goal and decision points kept by code; listing test bars at day 7, 14 and 21 | `5867280`, `5b0db88`; `agent/roadmap.py:349`, `agent/gates.py` |
| Venture stages on the agent's word | stage rules: research 21 d, triage 30 d, first test, live 60 d, scale | `570f31c`, `ab713b0`; `agent/stages.py` |
| "Use research sparingly", `DECIDE_USD` | $0.60 research budget per venture, repeat questions skipped | `cadb759` |
| Prose business case | numeric case (`econ.py`), knock-outs, critic, READY ranking | `4ced088`, `5603605`, `c79fa08`, `4bd68bd` |
| Handoff through the last reply | cycle digest; journal written by code | `441eb29` |
| Promises and "once a day" | obligations ledger; 2 messages a day | `18faa4f` |
| "The cap is there to be spent" | burn modes set from the net runway | `6a0231f`; `economy/burn.py:25-31` |
| Demand checks | a demand note is required before a product line's first listing | `1eadb12` |
| Every action waits for a click | policy engine, NEVER (code and DB), journal, Undo, digest | `c5c3fb6`, `c82893e`, `110f71a` |
| Photo thresholds (5–10 vs 3+) | one `qa.MIN_PHOTOS = 5` | `fb6127e`; `integrations/qa.py:21` |

**Still prompt-only (judgement).** Each item has a live consequence:
- **Is it any good?** Only "Look at the pictures of what you make" (`agent/prompts.py:94`) covers visual and design quality. Code counts photos. Live, the agent met the count with near-duplicates, and the owner said so on requests #12 and #13 ("additional pictures just seem like duplicates", B:1400-1401). This is Goodhart's law: move quality into code as a count, and the count becomes the target.
- **Which milestone a cycle aims at** (`focus_milestone_id`). This now decides both cost attribution and whether an unlock applies (§5). Nothing tells the planner the second part.
- **Sleep length.** The agent chose 420–600 minutes (#43, #45, #46). With the wake options off, an owner message waits that long unless he presses Wake now.
- **Memory drifts from code:**
  - `lessons.md` still says "Every Etsy listing needs 3+ photos" (B:1497), while code says 5;
  - it keeps "No idea gets a no" (B:1494);
  - `strategy.md` still says "Current priority: dropshipping" (B:1481), while POD is backed and burn mode focus forbids new ideas.
- **Also prompt-only:** how to use the owner's time, honesty, treating fetched text as data (backed by nonce tags in code), and the four text goals the agent wrote (#1–#4), which it grades itself.
- **Prompt size did not shrink.** An ordinary cycle's fixed prompt is 45.7 KB against 45.9 KB at 0.11.1 (patch note E4), and `prompts.py` grew from 29.1 KB to 42.2 KB (git). The room that moving rules to code freed went to new tools and sections.

---

## 4. What the owner still does by hand, and why

| Kind | Live evidence (B) | Why | Could code take it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Approvals** | 12 of 12 Etsy requests (6 listings, 6 edits). Where the creating cycle is visible (#8–#14), he decided 1–30 minutes after it ended (B:1399-1410) | Unlocks unused and mis-fitted (§5); the firsts are NEVER on purpose | Yes for reversible edits, pins and POD products after the first (§7) |
| **QA and art direction** | Messages #52, #55, #58 (photos, 3 times); comments on #12 and #13 ("duplicates"); #62 (poster must be "designful, colourful") | Quality is prompt-only; code counts photos. `make_image` is capped at 4 a cycle (lesson, B:1500) | Partly: a diversity check on photo sets, required photo kinds, a vision check before proposing |
| **Scheduling** | Wake now 3 times (09-29 15:19 and 15:43, 09-30 15:01); 3 pause/resume pairs on 09-29; both wake options off; daily cap $5→$7 and workshop cap $0.50→$1.50 between A and B; **reset the cost estimates** at 12:26 after the guard scaled workshop estimates ×4 (B:3465, 3472) | Owner wakes cost full cycles (§6). A 0.7% or 5× overrun stops a cycle and scales estimates, and only a human can undo that | Yes: coalesced reactive wakes, a cheap reply call, a guard that recalibrates |
| **Revenue and costs** | No orders yet. Automatic revenue off, no exchange rate (B:58; `integrations/etsy_revenue.py:75`). A reconcile-with-the-console warning for $0.10 of interrupted calls (B:245) | Trust boundary (only the owner or verified integrations record revenue) is right. Etsy fees are a button (`6f0fb1e`); Printify costs are a click per order (E4 deviation) | Turn on the automatic writer. Record Printify costs from the verified integration: a cost can't inflate the books |
| **Setup** | Printify account, token and Etsy link (#57); unconfirmed Printify and Pinterest confirmation emails (#60); Pinterest enabled without an app (B:77); website off; 4 Library documents (Etsy guides) | NEVER: accounts. DDG §5: Impressum. Both are legitimate | No. Make the cost visible in the venture case (owner hours) |
| **Strategy** | Backed #4, asked for research on #3, notes on #2–#4, standing instructions changed twice | By design: only the owner backs or kills | No |
| **Releases** | 8 restarts on 09-29, 6 on 09-30; marked upgrade #1 released | Development lives outside the agent | No, but release less often (§9) |

**Totals:**
- **09-29:** 27 panel actions, 6 pause/resume actions and 3 Wake now presses, 36 in all (44 with restarts). The first analysis counted about 46 a day with restarts, 33 without. Phase D's watch item was "under 10".
- **09-30 up to 17:10:** 10 panel actions and 1 Wake now press (6 restarts). The drop came mainly from sending 1 message instead of 12.

Nothing computes these numbers. I rebuilt them from the last 200 events.

---

## 5. The policy engine: usable as built?

**Sound, keep as is:**
- NEVER checked in code and again in the DB, with a 300-request agreement test (`agent/never.py:81-106`, migration 0051, `tests/test_never.py`);
- revocation on a veto, an unclear result, a spent budget, or a missed or dropped milestone (`agent/policy.py:304-347`);
- the journal and Undo (`integrations/connectors.py`, `agent/audit.py`);
- the switch that takes back every unlock;
- the first-publication rule: one click per new channel. For Etsy it has been met since 09-29. For Pinterest and Printify it is the right moment for the owner to accept the duties.

**Why the delegation half won't be used:**

1. **It is keyed to the plan's focus milestone.**
   - `store.insert_approval` stamps each request with the cycle's focus milestone (`agent/store.py:355-365`).
   - `policy.apply` looks only at that milestone's grant (`agent/policy.py:242-246`).
   - **Reproduced:** the owner unlocks `price_change` (auto) on milestone A, and the same listing gets the same 5% price cut. The request waits for the owner when the plan aimed at milestone B; it is approved at once when the plan aimed at A.
   - The planner is never told this. "Unlock" appears in no prompt or context; only CHANGELOG lines 40-51 mention it.
   - Live, the focus moved between #3 and #8 from cycle to cycle.
2. **Unlocks end quietly with their milestone.**
   - `apply` needs the milestone open (`policy.py:246`); revocation handles only missed or dropped milestones (`policy.py:322-325`).
   - **Reproduced:** after its milestone is closed done, the grant still reads `auto` in `policy.grants`, so the unlock counts in the sensors and the audit view still include it (`agent/service.py:850`, `agent/audit.py:503`). The next request waits.
   - Code-set milestones last 7 days (day-7 bars), 14 (scale) or 21 (first tests). **Success removes autonomy** instead of earning more.
3. **The rules don't match the requests.** The live requests (B:1399-1410):

   | Requests | Fits? |
   |---|---|
   | #3–#7: new listings (#3 was the shop's first publication; these were the first 5 of venture #1) | no (`listing_variant` needs 5 earlier unchanged approvals) |
   | #8: category fix | no (no rule) |
   | #9–#11: photos 1→3 | no (3 < `MIN_PHOTOS`) |
   | **#12–#13: photos 3→5** | **yes (`qa_fix`)** |
   | #14: new listing, project without a venture, text contains "Mietvertrag" and "Steuerberatung" | no (no venture; tax/contract filter) |

   **2 of 13 fit, even with perfect grants.** The next month's requests:
   - the day-7 bars (#9–#13, all due 10-07, views now 0–2 per line) will mostly be missed, and each miss is owed "fix titles, tags and category" (`agent/gates.py`), which no rule covers;
   - ≥3 Printify products for #8 and #2: the first is NEVER and no rule covers the rest;
   - pins: no rule (`policy.py:105-137` only knows email, etsy_edit and etsy_listing);
   - only the 4 photo fixes (2–3 → 5) fit.

   The owner has said he wants exactly the uncovered actions delegated: POD "perfect for you to research designs and create the items and listings by yourself", and Pinterest "I don't want to do it" (B:1341-1345).
4. **The tax/contract word filter catches product copy.** `never.legal` reads title, description and payload (`never.py:50-60, :102`).
   - Request #14 hits because of the disclaimer the daily review asked for: "keine Rechts- oder Steuerberatung".
   - **Reproduced:** a 5% price change whose reason says "inkl. MwSt" waits for the owner.
   - German landlord, budget and tax-planner niches, which are Ember's German edge, will always hit it.
5. **Promotions can't be reached.** They group by (rule, milestone) and need 5 unchanged approvals within 30 days (`policy.py:352-370`). With requests scattered over whichever milestone each plan aimed at, and only 4 photo fixes left to make, no live pattern gets there.
6. **The veto window is slower than this owner.** It is fixed at 12 hours (`policy.py:60`); he decides in minutes. It only helps overnight.
7. **Setting unlocks is a grid, and it wakes the agent.** 13 open milestones × 5 rules = 65 switches (`agent/views.py:382-386`). Each switch (`web.py:581`) and the take-back button (`web.py:592`) wakes a full cycle while `wake_on_decision` is on.

**Verdict (judgement):** as built, the owner will either never unlock anything, or unlock one milestone and see almost nothing carried. Re-key unlocks to **venture or product line × action class, with an end date**. Add rules for the requests that are coming. Make promotion a one-click offer on the approval card. **Tie variant autonomy to outcomes:** when code sets "Scale it" after a first order (`gates.py`), offer `listing_variant` for that product line then, not after 5 approvals.

---

## 6. The event model, and what the owner's switches say

**What the data shows (live, B events):**
- **09-28, 14:38–15:38:** 9 owner messages started 9 cycles, #16–#24, for $0.92 in total. From 21:06 on, messages no longer woke the agent, so `wake_on_message` was off.
- **09-30:**
  - 11:57: scheduled cycle #42 made requests #12–#14.
  - 12:00:59: the owner approved #14. The decision started cycle **#43, a venture cycle about POD research that had nothing to do with #14** (B:728-730), $0.56.
  - 12:01:59 and 12:02:22: the owner approved #12 and #13 during #43, which queued cycle **#44** (12:05:43). It spent **$2.00**, $1.84 of it on one workshop call estimated at $0.35, and was stopped.
  - 12:09: restart. Report A (12:10) shows `wake_on_decision: false` (A:109).
  - 12:26: the owner reset the cost estimates.
- The decision wake had been built at his request the day before ("don't idle while waiting for an approval"). His complaint was idling, and the sleep cut already answers it (`agent/service.py:662-673`).

**Code facts:**
- Any decided request counts as news, plain approvals included (`agent/news.py:224-235`).
- Knock-out overrides, unlock changes and take-back all wake the agent too (`web.py:420, 431, 561, 571, 581, 592, 630`).
- An owner wake is a **full** cycle; only `trigger == "event"` is reactive (`agent/loop.py:252-254`).
- Owner wakes are limited only by the one-minute gap; event wakes by 4 a day and 30 minutes (`agent/agenda.py:36-37`).

**Sound:**
- the agenda's write-once, deduplicated rows;
- the checks when the agent is dormant or out of money;
- the reactive cycle (≤5 work steps, no venture, review, study or critic);
- mail read between cycles;
- the sleep cut while requests wait.

**Not sound:**
1. **Two wake paths with opposite rules.** The owner's own path, which fires most often, is the unbounded and expensive one.
2. **No filter and no coalescing.** An approval that Ember's code carries out needs no reaction, yet starts a cycle. A burst of clicks starts cycle after cycle.
3. **Urgency is mis-set:**
   - `milestone_due` fires for every open milestone, code-graded ones included (`agenda.py:135-150`). That is 6 wake days in the next 3 weeks for bookkeeping.
   - Orders need no reaction: Etsy delivers downloads and Printify fulfils orders.
   - Only inquiries, replies and the owner's items are time-critical.
4. **The evening reserve** holds 20% of the cap ($1.40 at $7) until 20:00 for events that have never occurred (`economy/metering.py:103-106, 406-414`).
5. **Two mechanisms handle milestone dates:** the check wake (`service.py:596-611`) and the agenda.

**What the switches say (inferred):**
- He wants activity: a $7 cap and a 60-minute interval against the $1.50 and 240-minute defaults (`config.py:114, 125`).
- He wants to control when money is spent: wakes off, Wake now pressed deliberately (once 6 seconds after a message).
- He is conversational: 12 messages on 09-29. A plan → work → reflect cycle at $0.36–$2.00 is the wrong unit for answering a question.

**Fix:**
- Make owner items an agenda kind. Keep only messages, rejections, requests the owner carried out or that failed, and venture or milestone decisions.
- Coalesce them: about 10 minutes after the owner's last action.
- Run them as reactive cycles within the event cap.
- Answer messages with **one cheap reply call** (about $0.03–0.05, estimate), with `message_owner`, `obligation_done` and promises.
- Put a "wake now" box on each message.
- Make orders, favorites and code-graded due dates non-urgent.
- Scale the reserve by the events of the last 14 days.
- Use one mechanism for dates.

---

## 7. Where more autonomy is safe and valuable next, and where not

| Action | Risk | Undo | Value now | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Title, tags, category, description and photo edits of Ember's own live listings | own listing, no money, no new contact | Undo restores the before (`agent/audit.py`) | **High:** day-7 misses on 10-07 and 4 photo shortfalls | Unlock per venture: auto, ≤3 a day, one edit per listing every 7 days, only if QA passes |
| Creating a Printify product **unpublished** to read its real cost | nothing public | delete | **High:** margins are checked only after approval today, and the agent went through Gelato and back to Printify because it lacked base costs (#61–#63) | A free tool, no approval; the proposal carries real margins |
| Printify products after the first | public, physical goods (GPSR), IP | delete, which takes the listing down | **High:** the owner asked for it | Veto window per backed venture, ≤2 a day; margin check plus an IP/brand-word check |
| Pins after the first board | public, under the owner's account | delete | Medium, and only if the owner finishes setup | Auto ≤3 a day, only linking Ember's live listings |
| Deactivating own listings | removes a listing | renew ($0.20) | Low-medium (day-14 park) | The existing rule |
| Recording Etsy revenue and fees; Printify costs | books | corrections | High once sales come; the scale and money-goal rules read recorded revenue | Owner turns on automatic recording with a rate; code records Printify costs |

**Where not (judgement):**
- **Keep as they are:**
  - NEVER classes: accounts, first contacts, money, community posts, legal;
  - first publication per channel;
  - the first listing of a new product line (quality and reputation risk; a demand note isn't a quality check);
  - price experiments while there's no traffic (no signal);
  - policy or budget changes by the agent.
- **Not now:** email replies. There are no inquiries.
- **Keep `listing_variant` off until a product line has a sale.** More variants of unsold products is exactly what the first analysis warned against.

---

## 8. Simplify or remove

1. **Replace the two wake paths with one agenda**, and drop the options `wake_on_message` and `wake_on_decision` (§6).
2. **Replace the 5 hand-written matchers and the per-milestone grid.** Use per-venture grants of connector classes, with eligibility taken from the flags the connectors already have (reversible, no first contact, no money: `integrations/connectors.py:62-124`), plus QA and NEVER.
3. **Narrow `never.legal`** to requests that do something legal, not product copy. Keep the code and the DB view in step.
4. **Promotions per class and venture, on the approval card.**
5. **Roadmap hygiene.** There are 13 open milestones for 6 listings with 4 views. The agent's text goals overlap the code's (#2 with #8, #4 with the day-7 bars, #1 with #5). Refuse a text goal when a catalogue metric covers its measure.
6. **Freeze channels without an owner commitment.** The website is off and has no Impressum data. Pinterest is half set up and the owner won't run it. Keep the code, stop extending it, and park venture #2 unless he does the setup.
7. **Freeze the Phase C tooling** (case, critic, desk, predictions): 0 live uses so far, and burn mode focus turns most of it off anyway (`economy/burn.py`).
8. **Small fixes:**
   - The first digest said "carried out nothing" for 09-29 (B:3458), a day on which 8 approved Etsy actions ran; the journal only starts with 0.13.0 (`agent/audit.py:392-470`).
   - The unlock count includes grants on closed milestones.

---

## 9. Recommended sequence

**Now (this week, before the runway runs down):**
1. 👤 **Money plan.** The net runway is 18.3 days (B:413). By my arithmetic from `economy/life.py:383-402`, maintenance (<15 days: one $0.40 cycle a day, no venture cycles) arrives about 10-01 at the $7 cap, 10-03 at $5 a day, and about 10-15 at $3 a day. The backed POD test (#8, due 10-21) would stall: one workshop run costs $0.35–$1.84. Lower the cap to about $3 or top up the balance. Also decide Pinterest (do the setup or park #2), and turn on automatic revenue with a rate.
2. **Owner wakes through the agenda,** filtered, coalesced and reactive, plus the reply call (§6).
3. **Guard:** a small overrun on a workshop or server-tool call should recalibrate, not stop the cycle. The estimate scale should decay by itself, so no owner reset is needed. #46 was stopped by a 0.7% overrun before the poster was proposed (B:3449).

**Next (one behaviour release, then a 72-hour soak):**
4. Re-key unlocks. Attribute requests by the object they act on (listing → project → venture). Add an end date.
5. Add the rules `listing_edit`, `pod_product` (after the first) and `pin` (after the first board); a free unpublished Printify draft; a narrower tax/contract filter; promotions on the approval card.
6. QA: move from counting photos to judging them. A near-duplicate check (perceptual hash) on each photo set, required photo kinds, a vision check against a rubric before proposing a listing or design, and the owner's approval comments turned into checks.
7. Agenda urgency and reserve (§6). Fix the digest.
8. **An autonomy scorecard in the diagnostics, computed by code:**
   - owner actions a day, by kind;
   - share of cycles the owner triggered;
   - share of reversible outbound actions carried by unlocks;
   - Undo and veto rate;
   - QA complaints;
   - time to answer an owner message;
   - cost per reaction.

**Later:**
- Ring-fence a budget for a backed venture's first test, so it survives maintenance mode.
- A READY list for ordinary cycles.
- The roadmap-hygiene rule.
- A deterministic design renderer (HTML/CSS → PNG) instead of $0.35–$1.84 workshop runs. The owner asked for HTML/CSS; the agent had to fake it with PIL.

**Stop building:** new channels, Phase C additions, new owner options and prompt sections. No autonomy by prompt, and no relaxing NEVER.

**Watch (targets for the next analysis):**

| Metric | Target |
|---|---|
| Owner actions a day | under 10 |
| Owner-triggered cycles | under 15% |
| Reversible outbound actions carried by unlocks | at least 50%, within 2 weeks of granting |
| Undo and veto rate | under 10% |
| Owner QA complaints | 0–1 a week |
| Owner message answered (daytime) | under 30 minutes |
| Cost of a reaction | under $0.10 |

**For the other two reviews:**
- **Economics:** the runway drop into maintenance; the $1.84 workshop call (18% of all API spend); the planner call uncached at 11.5k tokens (B call #438).
- **Decision quality:** lessons and strategy that contradict code; four self-graded text goals.

recommendations.title: Decide the money plan before burn-mode maintenance stalls the backed POD test
recommendations.why: Net runway is 18.3 days (report B:413-415). Maintenance starts below 15 days (economy/burn.py:25-31): one scheduled cycle a day capped at $0.40, and no venture cycles. From economy/life.py:383-402 it arrives around 10-01 at the $7 cap, 10-03 at $5 a day, and 10-15 at $3 a day. One workshop run costs $0.35 to $1.84, so the backed venture's first test (milestone #8, due 10-21) would stall and could be parked by code once missed.
recommendations.how: Owner: lower the daily cap to about $3, or top up the balance. Code (small): show the projected date of the next burn-mode change on the STATUS line and the dashboard.

recommendations.title: Route the owner's own wake-ups through the agenda: filtered, coalesced and reactive
recommendations.why: Every decided request, knock-out override, unlock change and take-back wakes a full cycle (web.py:420,431,561,571,581,592,630; agent/news.py:224-235). Only 'event' cycles are lean (agent/loop.py:252-254). Live: 9 message wakes in 60 minutes on 09-28 (cycles #16-#24, $0.92). On 09-30, two approvals woke #43 ($0.56, a venture cycle unrelated to the approved request) and #44 ($2.00) within 8 minutes. The owner switched off both options each time (report A:109; B:130-131).
recommendations.how: Make owner items an agenda kind: messages, rejections, requests the owner carried out or that failed, and venture or milestone decisions. Leave out plain approvals that code executes, unlock changes and take-back. Wait until about 10 minutes after the owner's last action, then run one reactive cycle within the event cap. Replace wake_on_message and wake_on_decision with a 'wake now' box on each message.

recommendations.title: Stop the guard from ending a cycle over a small overrun on workshop or server-tool calls
recommendations.why: Cycle #46 was stopped because a workshop call cost $0.3466 against a $0.3441 estimate (report B:3449). The stop came at step 5 of 15, before the poster was proposed and without a reflection. #44 was stopped by a $1.84 call estimated at $0.35 (B:3472). The ×4 estimate scaling that followed had to be reset by the owner (B:3465). The worst case of a code-execution call can't be proven, so these stops will recur.
recommendations.how: For server-tool and workshop calls, treat an overrun below about 25% as a recalibration: log it and scale the estimate. Keep going if the cycle can still afford its reflection. Cap the scale factor and let it decay by itself, so no owner reset is needed. Keep the hard stop for plain calls and for the daily cap and balance.

recommendations.title: Turn on automatic Etsy revenue recording with an exchange rate
recommendations.why: It is off and no rate is set (report B:58; integrations/etsy_revenue.py:75). Each sale would then need 2 to 3 owner clicks (revenue, Etsy fees, Printify cost). The code's scale rule, the money goal and the P&L all read recorded revenue, so the loop from sales back to decisions waits on the owner's bookkeeping.
recommendations.how: Owner: set etsy_auto_record_revenue on and etsy_usd_per_eur to about 1.1. Code: record Printify order costs from the verified integration too (a cost can only lower the books).

recommendations.title: Key unlocks to the venture or product line and the action class, not the plan's focus milestone
recommendations.why: Requests take the cycle's focus milestone (agent/store.py:355-365), and policy.apply only reads that milestone's grant (agent/policy.py:242-246). Reproduced: with price_change unlocked on milestone A, an identical 5% price cut on the same listing was approved when the plan aimed at A and waited when it aimed at B. Once a milestone is met, its grant stops applying but still counts as an unlock (policy.py:246, 322-325; service.py:850). Code-set milestones last 7 to 21 days, so success removes autonomy.
recommendations.how: Grant per venture (or project) and connector class, with a daily limit, a budget of actions and an end date (default 30 days). Attribute each request by the object it acts on (listing to project to venture). Revoke on park or kill, an unclear result, a veto or a spent budget, as today. Keep NEVER and its DB checks unchanged. Remove the milestone-by-rule grid from the Roadmap tab.

recommendations.title: Add unlock rules for the requests of the next month: listing edits, POD products after the first, pins after the first board
recommendations.why: Only 2 of 13 live requests would have fit any rule (#12 and #13, photos 3 to 5; report B:1399-1410). The next month's requests fall outside the rules: title, tag and category fixes owed after the day-7 bars due 10-07 (agent/gates.py), Printify products, and pins (policy.py:105-137 knows only email, etsy_edit and etsy_listing). The owner asked for POD and Pinterest to be delegated (B:1341-1345).
recommendations.how: listing_edit: title, tags, category, description or photos of Ember's own live listing; QA must pass; at most one edit per listing every 7 days; Undo restores it. pod_product: in a backed venture, after the owner's first product; the margin check stays; add a brand-word and IP check; veto window, at most 2 a day. pin: after the first board, linking only Ember's live listings, at most 3 a day. Derive eligibility from the connector flags (reversible, no first contact, no money) plus QA and NEVER.

recommendations.title: Let Ember create a Printify product unpublished to read its real cost before asking
recommendations.why: The margin is checked only after the owner approves, so a failing product costs an approval and a retry (Phase E4 deviation). Without base costs the agent researched Gelato, recommended it, and was overruled back to Printify (messages #61-#63; cycles #43, #45, #46).
recommendations.how: A free tool: upload, create the product unpublished, read the making costs, keep it as a draft that is deleted after N days. The proposal then shows real margins per price. Publishing stays an approval or an unlock.

recommendations.title: Narrow the NEVER tax/contract word filter to legal acts, not product copy
recommendations.why: never.legal reads a request's title, description and payload (agent/never.py:50-60, 102). Live request #14 (the Nebenkostenabrechnung listing) hits 'Mietvertrag' and 'Steuerberatung', the latter from the disclaimer the daily review asked for. Reproduced: a 5% price change whose reason says 'inkl. MwSt' waits for the owner. German landlord, budget and tax-planner niches, Ember's German edge, will always hit it.
recommendations.how: Apply the filter to requests that do something legal (owner-only types, emails to authorities, request texts about filing or signing), or to the agent's reason and description only, not the listing payload. Change migration 0051's view the same way, and extend test_never's code/DB agreement test.

recommendations.title: Offer promotions on the approval card, per action class and venture, and tie variants to outcomes
recommendations.why: Promotions group by rule and milestone and need 5 unchanged approvals in 30 days (agent/policy.py:352-370). With requests spread over whichever milestone each plan aimed at, and only 4 photo fixes left, none can trigger. The 12-hour veto window (policy.py:60) is also far slower than this owner, who decides 1 to 30 minutes after the creating cycle ends.
recommendations.how: After 3 to 5 unchanged approvals of a class in a venture, the card offers 'let Ember do these (auto, 3 a day, 10 in all, 30 days)': one click. When code sets 'Scale it' after a first order (gates.py), offer listing_variant for that product line then, instead of counting approvals. Use auto with the daily digest and Undo for reversible classes; keep the veto window for the rest.

recommendations.title: Move quality, not counts, into code
recommendations.why: The owner did QA 5 times in 2 days: messages #52, #55 and #58 about photos, 'pictures seem like duplicates' on #12 and #13, and the poster design brief in #62. Code checks only a photo count (integrations/qa.py:21), which the agent met with near-duplicates. lessons.md still says 3+ photos while code says 5 (report B:1497). Visual quality is one prompt line (agent/prompts.py:94).
recommendations.how: A perceptual-hash diversity check across a listing's photo set. Required photo kinds (cover mockup, inside page, what's included, format and size). A cheap vision call that scores a listing or design against a rubric before proposing, as a code gate. Turn the owner's approval comments into obligations or checks. Drop memory lessons that contradict a code constant.

recommendations.title: Answer the owner's messages with one cheap reply call, not a full cycle
recommendations.why: The owner is conversational (12 messages on 09-29, 9 in one hour on 09-28). Today each answer costs a plan, work and reflect cycle: $0.36 to $2.00 in cycles #42-#46. With wakes off, a message waits for agent-chosen sleeps of 420 to 600 minutes unless he presses Wake now.
recommendations.how: A 'reply' purpose: one worker-model call with STATUS, OBLIGATIONS and the unread messages, and only the tools message_owner (with commits) and obligation_done. It runs within minutes of the coalesced owner event; the work itself follows in the next cycle. Estimated cost $0.03 to $0.05.

recommendations.title: Fix agenda urgency, the evening reserve and the double mechanism for milestone dates
recommendations.why: milestone_due is urgent for every open milestone, code-graded ones included (agent/agenda.py:135-150): 6 wake days in the next 3 weeks, for bookkeeping. Orders need no reaction (Etsy delivers downloads, Printify fulfils orders). The reserve holds 20% of the cap until 20:00 for events that haven't occurred (economy/metering.py:103-106, 406-414). Check wakes (service.py:596-611) duplicate the agenda.
recommendations.how: Keep inquiries, replies and owner items urgent. Make orders, favorites and code-graded due dates non-urgent (the next plan lists them). Scale the reserve by the events of the last 14 days (0 when there were none). Fold check wakes into the agenda.

recommendations.title: Compute an autonomy scorecard in code
recommendations.why: The Phase D watch items (owner actions under 10 a day, reaction under 60 minutes, 0 NEVER actions auto-approved) are measured nowhere; this review rebuilt them from the last 200 events. The first 0.13.0 digest said 'carried out nothing' for 09-29, a day when 8 approved Etsy actions ran, because the journal starts with 0.13.0 (agent/audit.py:392-470; report B:3458).
recommendations.how: A diagnostics and dashboard section: owner actions a day by kind, share of owner-triggered cycles, share of reversible outbound actions carried by unlocks, Undo and veto rate, owner QA complaints, time to answer an owner message, cost per reaction. Fix the digest wording for days before the journal existed, and count only unlocks that still apply.

recommendations.title: Ring-fence a budget for a backed venture's first test that survives maintenance mode
recommendations.why: Burn modes are the right survival rule, but maintenance forbids venture cycles and caps every cycle at $0.40 (economy/burn.py:25-31, 47-55). A test the owner backed would then starve and be parked by code for missing its date (agent/stages.py). The owner has no way to say 'fund this test with $X'.
recommendations.how: When the owner backs a venture, he sets a money budget for its first test. Ordinary cycles may spend it on that venture's work until the test's date, even in maintenance. The burn mode counts it, and it shows in FOCUS.

recommendations.title: Roadmap hygiene: require a metric when one fits, and limit the agent's text goals
recommendations.why: There are 13 open milestones for 6 listings with 4 views (report B:1350-1364). The agent's text goals overlap the code's: #2 '3 POD listings live' with #8, #4 '20 views' with the day-7 bars, #1 with the money goal #5. All 4 of its goals are self-graded.
recommendations.how: milestone_plan refuses a text measure when a catalogue metric covers it (views, listings live, orders, revenue), and caps the agent's open goals (for example 3).

recommendations.title: Don't build more channels or venture-decision tooling until a leg shows a signal
recommendations.why: 77 commits and 44 migrations landed in about 21 hours, and two behaviour releases were installed 6.5 hours apart. 0.13.0 added 3 channels, and only Printify is set up: Pinterest has no app and the owner won't run it; the website is off. The Phase C tables are all empty and focus mode turns most of that tooling off. 6 listings have 4 views in total.
recommendations.how: Freeze new channels, owner options, prompt sections and Phase C additions. Park venture #2 unless the owner finishes the Pinterest setup. Keep a 72-hour soak for every behaviour release, and judge them by the scorecard.

recommendations.title: Don't relax NEVER, first publication, or the owner's click on a new product line's first listing
recommendations.why: These rules are cheap (one click per channel or product line), legally grounded (UWG §7, DDG §5, Anthropic's usage policy on accounts) and double-checked in code and the DB (migration 0051, tests/test_never.py). A new line carries quality and reputation risk, which a demand note doesn't cover. The owner decides within minutes, so they cost little.
recommendations.how: Keep them. At most, allow a veto window for a new line in a leg that already has sales. Keep listing_variant off until the product line has sold.
